rationale: The complete Parkinson crossover compares atomoxetine with placebo on laboratory impulsivity, response inhibition and related cognitive tasks. Fig. in the article labels illustrations. The trial has no dried fig intervention or separate visual hallucination frequency result.

The original protocol plans three groups of Parkinson rehabilitation, rehabilitation with care assistant support, and usual care. Pain on a visual analogue scale is a planned secondary endpoint. No dried date comparison or outcome under fruit is specified.

The complete case report and its Table describe pulmonary infection and previous cases. Pleuritic pain was a presenting symptom in a patient without a Parkinson intervention. Date labels are calendar or bibliographic fields, with no fruit exposure.

The complete community Parkinson survey measures sleep using PDSS items and records dates of onset, diagnosis and therapy. Nighttime pain-related items are rest or sleep context and have no dried date exposure or isolated fruit effect.

The original V-TIME protocol compares treadmill training with and without virtual reality, with falls as the primary endpoint. Pain appears in exclusion criteria and broad quality-of-life measures. The falls calendar dates do not identify a food exposure.

The original surgical case describes severe back pain from a thoracic fracture and accompanying spinal cord impairment. Its comparisons concern fracture and postoperative course. It includes no dried date exposure or culinary comparison.

The original PROUD trial assigns pramipexole or placebo in the initial delayed-start phase. Back-pain counts appear in the adverse event table rather than a dried date pain-severity comparison. No date fruit was assigned.

The complete study compares neuropathy under intestinal levodopa infusion and oral Parkinson drugs. The body describes neuropathic pain by medication group, with no dried date intervention or separate dietary attribution.

The full GEDIMAplus protocol compares care management with usual care in people with diabetes and multimorbidity. Parkinson disease or chronic pain may contribute to eligibility. General diet self-care and dates of birth do not identify a dried date intervention.

This cross-sectional Parkinson study evaluates depression, activities of daily living and quality of life. Pain is mentioned in the clinical background. The observed associations give no dried date exposure or dedicated pain-severity contrast.

The complete randomized comparison evaluates extended- and immediate-release pramipexole. Upper abdominal pain appears as a reported adverse event in both drug groups. The outcome is separate from pain severity under dried date fruit.

The full imaging study compares needle conditions and brain responses to acupuncture at GB34. Pain literature and laboratory names are contextual. The article reports no dried date comparison and no corresponding change in pain severity.

The complete PERFORM article describes a sensor and reporting system. Its pain and discomfort maps are patient-entered monitoring fields. Device dates configure timing and calendars. No dried date exposure comparison was measured.

The full clinical principles article uses an illustrative case involving Parkinson symptoms and back pain. The discussion describes several treatment changes and reassessment. It includes no dried date exposure or interpretable fruit comparison.

The complete open-label intestinal levodopa study records abdominal and procedural pain as adverse events largely around device placement. These observations have no dried date exposure and do not estimate a culinary effect on Parkinson pain severity.

The original journal PDF reports apathy and executive testing in Parkinson dementia and Alzheimer groups. Anxiety is a distinct Neuropsychiatric Inventory subscale. Salmon occurs as a cited author surname and no poached salmon exposure or associated change in anxiety was tested.

The original journal title index maps SU212 to the recovered organizer abstract. The full 728-page book was screened and PDF pages 316–317 inspected. SU212 compares rotary vestibulo-ocular reflex gain by existing freezing status. Candidate herb matches are byline names. There is no fresh lemon balm comparison.
